---
title: "FMR guide: local Fusion Metadata Registry for the AFW 360 standard"
date: 2026-09-29
---

This guide records the real steps used on 2026-09-29 (work package WP8b) to
run the Fusion Metadata Registry (FMR) locally on Windows 11 without
administrator rights or Docker, and the workflow for loading, validating and
editing the AFW 360 structures. The research behind it, with sources, is in
`tools/fmr/README.md`.

::: {.callout-note}
## Status: load, validation and round trip work through the SDMX-ML 3.0 profile

FMR 12.4.2 does not read SDMX-ML 3.1, so `tools/fmr/fmr_load.R` loads the
SDMX-ML 3.0 profile that `pipeline/build_sdmx.R --sdmx-ml-version 3.0`
writes to `tmp/fmr/v30/` (same artefacts, `v3_0` namespaces, without the
metadata structure, metadataflow and metadata provision agreement). The
3.1 file under `sdmx/` stays the canonical committed output. The data files
in `data/` (SDMX-CSV 2.1) validate without change, and the structures
exported back from FMR (SDMX-ML 3.0) give an empty
`pipeline/import_sdmx.R --diff`. See [Workflow](#workflow).
:::

::: {.callout-warning collapse="true"}
## Why the 3.0 profile: FMR 12.4.2 rejects the SDMX-ML 3.1 structure message

Loading `sdmx/structures/AFW360_structures.xml`
(SDMX-ML 3.1, `v3_1` namespaces) fails. Response of
`POST /ws/secure/sdmxapi/rest/`, both as a multipart upload
(`-F uploadFile=@...`) and as a raw `application/xml` body:

```
HTTP 400
<message:Error xmlns:message="http://www.sdmx.org/resources/sdmxml/schemas/v2_1/message" ...>
  <message:ErrorMessage code="150">
    <com:Text>Unrecognised file format, contents of file are: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<mes:Structure xmlns:mes="http://www.sdmx.org/resources/sdmxml/schemas/v3_1/message" xmlns:str="http://www.sdmx.org/resources/sdmxml/schemas/v3_1/structure" ...
```

FMR log (`tools/fmr/runtime/tomcat/logs/FusionRegistryWarnings.log`):

```
ERROR http-nio-8080-exec-7 io.sdmx.format.ml.engine.error.ErrorWriterEngineV21 - Unrecognised file format, contents of file are: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
```

FMR's documentation lists SDMX-ML up to 3.0; the 3.1 namespaces are not
recognised at all (the error body itself is SDMX-ML 2.1). Following the plan's
contingency (section 2.13), WP8b2 added the `--sdmx-ml-version 3.0` option to
`pipeline/build_sdmx.R`. With the 3.0 profile the format error is gone and
the only remaining obstacle was the agency `WB` (see step 2 of the workflow).
:::

## What is installed

Everything lives under `tools/fmr/runtime/` (gitignored); nothing is written
to the registry, services or the user profile.

| Component | Version | Location | Port |
|---|---|---|---|
| Java | Azul Zulu 21.0.12.1 (already on `PATH`, `JAVA_HOME`) | `C:\Program Files\Zulu\zulu-21` | |
| Apache Tomcat | 10.1.60 (Windows zip) | `tools/fmr/runtime/tomcat` | 8080 (HTTP), 8015 (shutdown) |
| FMR | 12.4.2 (`fmr-12.4.2.war`, 129,151,617 bytes) | `tools/fmr/runtime/tomcat/webapps/ROOT.war` | served at `/` |
| MySQL | 8.0.46 (noinstall zip, MD5 checked) | `tools/fmr/runtime/mysql`, data in `mysql/data` | 3306, `127.0.0.1` only |
| MySQL Connector/J | 9.6.0 | `tools/fmr/runtime/tomcat/lib/mysql-connector-j-9.6.0.jar` | |

- Downloads are kept in `tools/fmr/runtime/dl/`, logs of the two processes in
  `tools/fmr/runtime/logs/`, Tomcat and FMR logs in
  `tools/fmr/runtime/tomcat/logs/` (`FusionRegistry.log`,
  `FusionRegistryWarnings.log`).
- Java heap: `-Xmx16g` (the FMR wiki's value; the machine has 128 GB).
- Database `fmr` (utf8mb4), user `fmruser@localhost`. MySQL `root` has no
  password and listens on `127.0.0.1` only.
- FMR superuser: `root`. Passwords (database user and FMR superuser) are in
  `tools/fmr/runtime/secrets.txt`, never committed.
- FMR's home folder and `fmr.properties` are in `tools/fmr/runtime/home/`
  (set through `-Duser.home` and `-DRegistryProperties`).

## Install steps (as run)

Commands run from the repository root; Git Bash unless marked PowerShell.

1. Check resources: free disk space, RAM and ports
   (`netstat -ano | findstr LISTENING`). Port 8005, Tomcat's default shutdown
   port, was taken by a system process, so the shutdown port is 8015.

2. Download into `tools/fmr/runtime/dl/` (curl needs `--ssl-no-revoke` on
   this machine):

   ```sh
   curl --ssl-no-revoke -sSLO https://dlcdn.apache.org/tomcat/tomcat-10/v10.1.60/bin/apache-tomcat-10.1.60.zip
   curl --ssl-no-revoke -sSLO https://github.com/bis-med-it/fmr-public/releases/download/v12.4.2/fmr-12.4.2.war
   curl --ssl-no-revoke -sSLO https://dev.mysql.com/get/Downloads/MySQL-8.0/mysql-8.0.46-winx64.zip
   curl --ssl-no-revoke -sSLO https://dev.mysql.com/get/Downloads/Connector-J/mysql-connector-j-9.6.0.zip
   ```

   Check the Tomcat zip against its `.sha512` file on `downloads.apache.org`,
   the WAR size against the GitHub release (129,151,617 bytes), and the MySQL
   zip's MD5 against the MySQL download page.

3. Unzip (PowerShell `Expand-Archive`) to `tools/fmr/runtime/tomcat` and
   `tools/fmr/runtime/mysql`; copy the Connector/J jar to
   `tools/fmr/runtime/tomcat/lib/` (Tomcat's own `lib`, because the database
   connection is a Tomcat JNDI resource).

4. MySQL: write `tools/fmr/runtime/mysql/my.ini`:

   ```ini
   [mysqld]
   basedir=<repo>/tools/fmr/runtime/mysql
   datadir=<repo>/tools/fmr/runtime/mysql/data
   port=3306
   bind-address=127.0.0.1
   mysqlx=OFF
   log-error=<repo>/tools/fmr/runtime/logs/mysqld.err
   [client]
   port=3306
   host=127.0.0.1
   ```

   then initialise the data directory, start the server (see below) and
   create the database:

   ```sh
   tools/fmr/runtime/mysql/bin/mysqld --defaults-file=tools/fmr/runtime/mysql/my.ini --initialize-insecure
   tools/fmr/runtime/mysql/bin/mysql --defaults-file=tools/fmr/runtime/mysql/my.ini -u root -e \
     "CREATE DATABASE fmr CHARACTER SET utf8mb4;
      CREATE USER 'fmruser'@'localhost' IDENTIFIED BY '<password>';
      GRANT ALL ON fmr.* TO 'fmruser'@'localhost'; FLUSH PRIVILEGES;"
   ```

5. Tomcat configuration:
   - `conf/server.xml`: `<Server port="8015" shutdown="SHUTDOWN">`.
   - `conf/context.xml`: add, inside `<Context>`, the JNDI resource from the
     FMR wiki's Jndi page:

     ```xml
     <Resource name="fmrdatabase" auth="Container" type="javax.sql.DataSource"
       driverClassName="com.mysql.cj.jdbc.Driver"
       url="jdbc:mysql://127.0.0.1:3306/fmr?allowPublicKeyRetrieval=true&amp;useSSL=false"
       username="fmruser" password="<password>"
       maxTotal="10" minIdle="5" maxWaitMillis="-1"
       timeBetweenEvictionRunsMillis="7200000" minEvictableIdleTimeMillis="3600000"
       defaultAutoCommit="false" />
     ```

   - `bin/setenv.bat`:

     ```bat
     set "JAVA_OPTS=%JAVA_OPTS% -Xmx16g -Duser.home=<repo>/tools/fmr/runtime/home -DRegistryProperties=file:///<repo>/tools/fmr/runtime/home/fmr.properties"
     ```

   - Copy `fmr-12.4.2.war` to `webapps/ROOT.war` and delete the default
     `webapps/ROOT` folder, so FMR is served at `http://localhost:8080/`.

6. Start Tomcat (see below). The first start takes about two minutes while
   the WAR unpacks; `http://localhost:8080/` then redirects to
   `/install.html`.

7. First-run setup. In a browser: open `http://localhost:8080/`, accept the
   licence, choose *JNDI connection* with JNDI name `fmrdatabase`, context
   `java:/comp/env`, driver `com.mysql.cj.jdbc.Driver`, server URL
   `http://localhost:8080`, superuser `root` and a password. The same steps
   without a browser (the calls the setup page makes; a session cookie from
   `install.html` is required, otherwise the calls return 401):

   ```sh
   B=http://localhost:8080/ws/secure/settings
   C="-s -c tmp/fmr/cj -b tmp/fmr/cj -H Content-Type:application/json"
   curl $C -o /dev/null http://localhost:8080/install.html
   curl $C -X POST $B/saveLicenceAgreement
   curl $C -d '{"jndiName":"fmrdatabase","jndiContext":"java:/comp/env","driver":"com.mysql.cj.jdbc.Driver"}' $B/saveDatabaseSettings
   curl $C -d 'http://localhost:8080' $B/saveServerUrl
   curl $C -d 'Fusion Metadata Registry' $B/saveRegistryName
   curl $C -d '{"username":"root","password":"<password>","maxLoginAttempts":"-1"}' $B/saveRootSecuritySettings
   curl $C -X POST $B/completeInstall
   ```

   Each call returns `{"Success":[true]}`. Afterwards
   `http://localhost:8080/` returns 200 and the `fmr` database holds 34 tables.

## Start and stop

Start MySQL, then Tomcat (PowerShell, from anywhere; both run hidden as the
current user, output in `tools/fmr/runtime/logs/`):

```powershell
$r = "C:\Users\wb532966\eb-local\AFW360_Glance\tools\fmr\runtime"
Start-Process -FilePath "$r\mysql\bin\mysqld.exe" -ArgumentList "--defaults-file=`"$r\mysql\my.ini`"" -RedirectStandardOutput "$r\logs\mysqld.out" -RedirectStandardError "$r\logs\mysqld.stderr" -WindowStyle Hidden
$env:CATALINA_HOME = "$r\tomcat"; $env:CATALINA_BASE = "$r\tomcat"; $env:JAVA_HOME = "C:\Program Files\Zulu\zulu-21"
Start-Process -FilePath "$r\tomcat\bin\catalina.bat" -ArgumentList "run" -WorkingDirectory "$r\tomcat" -RedirectStandardOutput "$r\logs\tomcat.out" -RedirectStandardError "$r\logs\tomcat.err" -WindowStyle Hidden
```

Ready when `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" http://localhost:8080/`
prints 200 (about two minutes).

Stop Tomcat, then MySQL:

```powershell
$r = "C:\Users\wb532966\eb-local\AFW360_Glance\tools\fmr\runtime"
$env:CATALINA_HOME = "$r\tomcat"; $env:CATALINA_BASE = "$r\tomcat"; $env:JAVA_HOME = "C:\Program Files\Zulu\zulu-21"
& "$r\tomcat\bin\shutdown.bat"
& "$r\mysql\bin\mysqladmin.exe" "--defaults-file=$r\mysql\my.ini" -u root shutdown
```

## Workflow

All commands run from the repository root in Git Bash, with FMR started
(see [Start and stop](#start-and-stop)). The scripts use the R packages
`curl` and `jsonlite`. The FMR address comes from `FMR_BASE` (default
`http://localhost:8080`); the account used to load structures comes from
`FMR_USER` and `FMR_PASSWORD`, or else from `tools/fmr/runtime/secrets.txt`
(`FMR_ADMIN_USER`, `FMR_ADMIN_PASSWORD`). Every response is kept under
`tmp/fmr/`.

### 1. Generate the SDMX files

```sh
Rscript pipeline/build_sdmx.R --root .
```

This writes the canonical SDMX-ML 3.1 message under `sdmx/`. It is not what
FMR loads (see the status box); step 2 builds the 3.0 profile itself.

### 2. Load the structures

```sh
Rscript tools/fmr/fmr_load.R --root .
```

The script runs four steps:

1. **FMR up?** `GET <FMR_BASE>/` must return 200.
2. **Register the agency `WB`, once.** The structure message declares the
   sub-agency `WB.AFW360` in the agency scheme `WB:AGENCIES(1.0)`. FMR can
   only store that scheme when the top-level agency `WB` exists in its own
   scheme `SDMX:AGENCIES(1.0)`; otherwise the load fails with

   ```
   HTTP 404, error code 100: Could not resolve reference from structure
   Agency Scheme 'WB:AGENCIES(1.0)' to structure Agency
   'urn:sdmx:org.sdmx.infomodel.base.Agency=SDMX:AGENCIES(1.0).WB'
   ```

   The script reads `GET /sdmx/v2/structure/agencyscheme/SDMX/AGENCIES/1.0`
   and, only when `WB` is missing, submits `tools/fmr/agencies_bootstrap.xml`
   (a SDMX-ML 3.0 message holding `SDMX:AGENCIES(1.0)` with the items `SDMX`
   and `WB`) to the same endpoint as step 4. The FMR superuser account from
   the install has the rights for this; no UI step is needed. On a fresh FMR
   the scheme holds only `SDMX`, which the bootstrap keeps. Response saved to
   `tmp/fmr/agencies_response.xml`. In the web interface the same is done
   under *Agencies* by adding `WB` to the top-level scheme.
3. **Build the SDMX-ML 3.0 profile:**

   ```sh
   Rscript pipeline/build_sdmx.R --root . --sdmx-ml-version 3.0 --out-root tmp/fmr/v30
   ```

   writes `tmp/fmr/v30/sdmx/structures/AFW360_structures.xml`: the 22
   codelists, concept scheme, data structure, dataflow, provision agreement
   and agency and provider schemes with `v3_0` namespaces; no metadata
   structure, metadataflow or metadata provision agreement (their 3.0 XML
   differs).
4. **Load it:** `POST /ws/secure/sdmxapi/rest/` with the file as the
   `application/xml` body, header `ACTION: REPLACE` (option `--action`) and
   HTTP Basic authentication. The response is saved to
   `tmp/fmr/load_response.xml`. The script exits 0 on HTTP 200 and prints
   `Success` when FMR reports stored structures. A repeated load of an
   unchanged message returns HTTP 200 with an empty
   `SubmitStructureResponse` (nothing to replace), printed as `HTTP 200`.

`Rscript tools/fmr/fmr_load.R --root . --file <message.xml>` skips steps 2
and 3 and loads the given message. The same load is possible in the web
interface (*Load Structures*), with the 3.0 profile.

### 3. Validate the data

```sh
Rscript tools/fmr/fmr_validate.R --root .
```

Each `data/AFW360_HH_*_SURVEY.csv` is POSTed unchanged to
`POST /ws/public/data/validate` (no login needed) with
`Content-Type: application/vnd.sdmx.data+csv;version=2.1.0`. FMR answers
with a JSON report, saved as `tmp/fmr/<ISO3>_<YEAR>_SURVEY_validation.json`.
The script prints one line per file and exits 0 only when every report says
`"Errors": false` and lists no error entries. Result on 2026-09-29:

```
AFW360_HH_GNB_2021_SURVEY.csv: HTTP 200, format SDMX CSV v2.0, dataflow WB.AFW360:AFW360_HH(0.3.0), 2268 observations, Errors: false, error entries: 0
AFW360_HH_SEN_2021_SURVEY.csv: HTTP 200, format SDMX CSV v2.0, dataflow WB.AFW360:AFW360_HH(0.3.0), 3003 observations, Errors: false, error entries: 0
```

FMR reads the SDMX-CSV 2.1 files as it reads SDMX-CSV 2.0 (the report's
`FileFormat` says `SDMX CSV v2.0`): the header `STRUCTURE,STRUCTURE_ID,ACTION,...`
is the same in both versions and the files use no 2.1-only feature. The data
files need no change.

### 4. Export and round trip

```sh
Rscript tools/fmr/fmr_export.R --root . --out tmp/fmr/export.xml
Rscript pipeline/import_sdmx.R --root . --diff tmp/fmr/export.xml
```

`fmr_export.R` GETs `/sdmx/v2/structure/*/WB,WB.AFW360/*/*?detail=full`,
every artefact maintained by `WB` (the scheme `WB:AGENCIES`) or `WB.AFW360`.
It asks for SDMX-ML 3.1 first; FMR 12.4.2 answers HTTP 406, so the script
takes SDMX-ML 3.0 (`v3_0` namespaces), which `import_sdmx.R` reads. With
the structures loaded as in step 2, the diff prints nothing on standard
output: FMR returns every code, name, description and annotation that the
CSVs under `metadata/` hold. `import_sdmx.R` notes on standard error that
`CL_FIGURE`, `CL_SOURCE` and `CL_SURVEY` are derived from registries and are
reported, not written; that is expected. What does not travel: the metadata
structure, metadataflow and metadata provision agreement (not in the 3.0
profile, so not in FMR), and the message header (FMR writes its own ID and
sender).

### 5. Edit structures in FMR

In FMR, work on a copy versioned `<next>-draft`; export it (step 4); run
`Rscript pipeline/import_sdmx.R --root . --diff <export.xml>` to see the
changes against the CSVs, then `--apply`; commit through a pull request; at
release, bump `metadata/VERSION`, regenerate (step 1) and reload (step 2).

### 6. Validation-only use

Steps 1 to 3.

## Findings from the install

- FMR 12.4.2 runs on Azul Zulu 21 (not named as tested by the vendor) and
  Tomcat 10.1.60 with MySQL 8.0.46 and Connector/J 9.6.0.
- FMR rejects SDMX-ML 3.1 structure messages (error 150, status box) and
  does not offer 3.1 on export (HTTP 406); it loads and exports SDMX-ML 3.0.
- FMR needs the top-level agency `WB` in `SDMX:AGENCIES(1.0)` before any
  `WB.AFW360` structure loads; `fmr_load.R` registers it when missing.
- FMR accepts the SDMX-CSV 2.1 data files as they are and reports them as
  SDMX-CSV 2.0.
- FMR's error and submission responses are SDMX-ML 2.1 documents, whatever
  the version of the message sent.
- FMR's default home folder is `<user home>\SDMX_IO\FMR`; with
  `-Duser.home` and `-DRegistryProperties` set as above, the only file it
  writes there, the generated `fmr.properties`, lands in
  `tools/fmr/runtime/home/`, and no `SDMX_IO` folder appears in the user
  profile. FMR's own logs go to `tools/fmr/runtime/tomcat/logs/`.
- The setup page's calls need a session cookie from `install.html`; without
  it they return HTTP 401.
